beginner.summary: For developers, system administrators and SRE or DevOps engineers who are new to Grafana Loki and need to collect, search and alert on logs. Covers how Loki indexes only labels and stores compressed chunks, a local Loki, Grafana Alloy and Grafana lab, log streams and labels, the push API and logcli, file, Docker, journal and Kubernetes collection with Alloy, moving from the deprecated Promtail to Alloy, LogQL log and metric queries, Grafana Explore, Logs Drilldown and dashboards, the Loki configuration file, label cardinality, first log-based alerts and a centralised logging capstone.
prerequisites: Uses a Linux shell confidently: files, pipes, curl, environment variables and reading application log files
Has run containers with Docker and Docker Compose and can read YAML configuration
Has a laptop with Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, 8 GB of RAM free for the lab and rights to open ports 3000, 3100 and 12345 locally
outcomes: Run Loki, Grafana Alloy and Grafana locally and explain how Loki stores logs as labelled streams of compressed chunks
Collect logs from files, Docker containers, the systemd journal and Kubernetes pods with Alloy pipelines that set a small, stable label set
Write LogQL log queries with selectors, line filters, parsers and label filters, and metric queries with range aggregations
Build Grafana dashboards and Grafana-managed alert rules on the Loki data source for a working application

advanced.summary: For platform engineers, SREs and architects who run or design Loki at large scale, for many tenants or alongside Grafana Cloud Logs.
